# Goal

Test whether the tuned three-step spatial-similarity method recovers the
paper-supported Day0 → Day9 fibroblast polarization linkages (Cadinu et al. 2024,
Cell), using a **full paired-slice** design:

* Each of the **10 Healthy Day0 slices** is paired with each of the **21
  DSS9/Day9 slices** → up to **10 × 21 = 210 slice-pair comparisons**.
* For every slice pair we build a directional similarity matrix with
  **rows = Day0 fibroblast types** and **columns = Day9 fibroblast/IAF types**.
* The readout is the **row-wise rank (and normalized rank) of each cognate Day9
  target among ALL Day9 candidate cell types** — i.e. for the Day0 origin, where
  does its paper-predicted Day9 partner land in the ranked candidate list.

Ground-truth linkages (all PDF-affirmed, location-preserving polarizations):

| Day0 origin (row) | Day9 target (column) | Compartment |
|---|---|---|
| **Fibro 6** | **IAF 2** | crypt base (MU) |
| **Fibro 2** | **IAF 4** | crypt top (MU) |
| **Fibro 7** | **Fibro 4** | submucosa (SM/ME) |

```{r libs}
library(dplyr); library(readr); library(stringr); library(tibble)
library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)
```

# Configuration and engine (tuned method)

```{r config-engine}
per_slice_xyt_dir <- c(
  Sys.getenv("COORD_DIR", ""),               # explicit override
  "output_threelayer/per_slice_morphogam",
  "../output_threelayer/per_slice_morphogam"
) %>% { .[which(nzchar(.) & dir.exists(.))[1]] }
stopifnot(!is.na(per_slice_xyt_dir))

layers <- c("MU", "SM", "ME")
CFG <- list(min_cells = 30, bw_mult = 2, bw_floor = 0.05, grid_n = 512,
            sigma_quantile = 0.5, gamma = 1)

# read fibroblast-lineage cells (Tier1 == Fibroblast covers Fibro* AND IAF*)
read_fibro <- function(slice_id, prefix) {
  bind_rows(lapply(layers, function(ly) {
    f <- file.path(per_slice_xyt_dir,
                   paste0(prefix, "_per_slice_", slice_id, "_", ly, "_xyt_mapped.csv"))
    if (!file.exists(f)) return(tibble())
    read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  })) %>%
    mutate(Slice_ID = as.character(Slice_ID), layer = as.character(layer),
           Tier1 = as.character(Tier1), Tier2 = as.character(Tier2),
           r_for_jsd = as.numeric(r_for_jsd)) %>%
    filter(Slice_ID == slice_id, layer %in% layers,
           grepl("fibro", Tier1, ignore.case = TRUE),
           is.finite(r_for_jsd), r_for_jsd >= 0, r_for_jsd <= 1) %>%
    transmute(layer, Tier2, value = r_for_jsd)
}

js_dist_kde <- function(x, y, bw, grid_n = 512) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]; y <- y[is.finite(y)]
  if (length(x) < 2 || length(y) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  dx <- density(x, bw = bw, from = 0, to = 1, n = grid_n)$y
  dy <- density(y, bw = bw, from = 0, to = 1, n = grid_n)$y
  px <- dx / sum(dx); py <- dy / sum(dy); m <- 0.5 * (px + py)
  kl <- function(p, q) { i <- p > 0 & q > 0; sum(p[i] * log(p[i] / q[i])) }
  sqrt(0.5 * kl(px, m) + 0.5 * kl(py, m))
}

# THREE-STEP ENGINE (optimised; named-vector lookups so 210 calls are fast).
# dat: layer, Tier2, value, grp ("A"=Day0 rows, "B"=Day9 cols).
# query_rows: restrict Day0 rows to these types (we only need the 3 origins).
three_step <- function(dat, cfg, query_rows = NULL, col_order = NULL) {
  A <- dat %>% filter(grp == "A"); B <- dat %>% filter(grp == "B")

  # ---- Step 1: per-layer KDE/JSD similarity ----
  per_layer <- function(ln) {
    dA <- A %>% filter(layer == ln); dB <- B %>% filter(layer == ln)
    rs <- dA %>% count(Tier2, name = "n") %>% filter(n >= cfg$min_cells) %>% pull(Tier2)
    cs <- dB %>% count(Tier2, name = "n") %>% filter(n >= cfg$min_cells) %>% pull(Tier2)
    if (!is.null(query_rows)) rs <- intersect(rs, query_rows)
    rs <- sort(rs); cs <- sort(cs)
    D <- matrix(NA_real_, length(rs), length(cs), dimnames = list(rs, cs))
    if (!length(rs) || !length(cs)) return(list(S = D))
    rA <- split(dA$value, dA$Tier2); rB <- split(dB$value, dB$Tier2)
    bw <- bw.nrd0(c(dA$value, dB$value)) * cfg$bw_mult
    if (!is.finite(bw) || bw <= 0) bw <- cfg$bw_floor
    for (i in rs) for (j in cs) D[i, j] <- js_dist_kde(rA[[i]], rB[[j]], bw, cfg$grid_n)
    sig <- as.numeric(quantile(D, cfg$sigma_quantile, na.rm = TRUE))
    if (!is.finite(sig) || sig <= 0) sig <- 1
    list(S = exp(-D / sig))
  }
  J <- setNames(lapply(layers, per_layer), layers)
  ar <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(J, function(x) rownames(x$S)))))
  ac <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(J, function(x) colnames(x$S)))))
  if (!length(ar) || !length(ac)) return(NULL)

  # ---- Step 2: cell-count-weighted layer integration ----
  Acnt <- A %>% count(layer, Tier2, name = "n"); Bcnt <- B %>% count(layer, Tier2, name = "n")
  AcL <- lapply(split(Acnt, Acnt$layer), function(d) setNames(d$n, d$Tier2))
  BcL <- lapply(split(Bcnt, Bcnt$layer), function(d) setNames(d$n, d$Tier2))
  Sn <- matrix(0, length(ar), length(ac), dimnames = list(ar, ac)); Sd <- Sn
  for (ly in layers) {
    S <- J[[ly]]$S; if (!length(rownames(S)) || !length(colnames(S))) next
    av <- AcL[[ly]]; bv <- BcL[[ly]]
    for (i in rownames(S)) for (j in colnames(S)) {
      s <- S[i, j]; if (!is.finite(s)) next
      ni <- av[i]; nj <- bv[j]; if (is.na(ni) || is.na(nj)) next
      w <- sqrt(ni * nj); if (!is.finite(w) || w <= 0) next
      Sn[i, j] <- Sn[i, j] + w * s; Sd[i, j] <- Sd[i, j] + w
    }
  }
  Ss <- Sn / Sd; Ss[Sd == 0] <- NA

  # ---- Step 3: layer-distribution overlap correction ----
  Ap <- Acnt %>% group_by(Tier2) %>% mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
  Bp <- Bcnt %>% group_by(Tier2) %>% mutate(p = n / sum(n)) %>% ungroup()
  ApT <- lapply(split(Ap, Ap$Tier2), function(d) setNames(d$p, d$layer))
  BpT <- lapply(split(Bp, Bp$Tier2), function(d) setNames(d$p, d$layer))
  LO <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow(Ss), ncol(Ss), dimnames = dimnames(Ss))
  for (i in rownames(Ss)) for (j in colnames(Ss)) {
    pa <- ApT[[i]]; pb <- BpT[[j]]; tot <- 0
    for (ly in layers) {
      va <- pa[ly]; vb <- pb[ly]
      va <- ifelse(is.na(va), 0, va); vb <- ifelse(is.na(vb), 0, vb)
      tot <- tot + sqrt(va * vb)
    }
    LO[i, j] <- tot
  }
  M <- Ss * (LO ^ cfg$gamma)
  ro <- if (is.null(query_rows)) rownames(M) else
    c(intersect(query_rows, rownames(M)), setdiff(rownames(M), query_rows))
  co <- if (is.null(col_order)) colnames(M) else
    c(intersect(col_order, colnames(M)), setdiff(colnames(M), col_order))
  M[ro, co, drop = FALSE]
}

# row-wise rank of `cand` among ALL finite candidates in row `q` (1 = best)
row_rank <- function(S, q, cand) {
  if (is.null(S) || !(q %in% rownames(S))) return(c(rank = NA, sim = NA, n = NA))
  v <- S[q, ]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]
  if (!(cand %in% names(v))) return(c(rank = NA, sim = NA, n = length(v)))
  c(rank = unname(rank(-v, ties.method = "min")[cand]), sim = unname(v[cand]), n = length(v))
}
# same, but excluding one column (used to drop the same-name Day9 persister)
row_rank_excl <- function(S, q, cand, excl) {
  if (is.null(S) || !(q %in% rownames(S))) return(c(rank = NA, n = NA))
  v <- S[q, ]; v <- v[is.finite(v)]; v <- v[setdiff(names(v), excl)]
  if (!(cand %in% names(v))) return(c(rank = NA, n = length(v)))
  c(rank = unname(rank(-v, ties.method = "min")[cand]), n = length(v))
}
```

```{r ground-truth}
gt <- tibble::tribble(
  ~origin,    ~cognate,  ~compartment,
  "Fibro 6",  "IAF 2",   "crypt base (MU)",
  "Fibro 2",  "IAF 4",   "crypt top (MU)",
  "Fibro 7",  "Fibro 4", "submucosa (SM/ME)"
)
col_order_d9 <- c("Fibro 6", "Fibro 13", "Fibro 2", "IAF 2", "IAF 3", "IAF 4",
                  "Fibro 7", "Fibro 4", "Fibro 5", "Fibro 12", "Fibro 1",
                  "Fibro 15", "Pericyte 1", "Pericyte 2", "IAF 1", "FRC")
```

# Load and cache all slices

```{r load}
day0_slices <- list.files(per_slice_xyt_dir,
  pattern = "^Healthy_all_per_slice_.*_MU_xyt_mapped\\.csv$") %>%
  str_remove("^Healthy_all_per_slice_") %>% str_remove("_MU_xyt_mapped\\.csv$") %>%
  unique() %>% { .[str_detect(., "_D0_")] } %>% sort()
day9_slices <- list.files(per_slice_xyt_dir,
  pattern = "^DSS9_all_per_slice_.*_MU_xyt_mapped\\.csv$") %>%
  str_remove("^DSS9_all_per_slice_") %>% str_remove("_MU_xyt_mapped\\.csv$") %>%
  unique() %>% sort()

day0_by_slice <- setNames(lapply(day0_slices, read_fibro, prefix = "Healthy_all"), day0_slices)
day9_by_slice <- setNames(lapply(day9_slices, read_fibro, prefix = "DSS9_all"), day9_slices)

cat(sprintf("Day0 slices: %d   Day9 slices: %d   →  up to %d slice-pair comparisons\n",
            length(day0_slices), length(day9_slices),
            length(day0_slices) * length(day9_slices)))
```

# Full paired-slice computation (10 × 21)

```{r paired-run}
pairs_grid <- expand.grid(d0 = day0_slices, d9 = day9_slices, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

paired <- pmap_dfr(pairs_grid, function(d0, d9) {
  datp <- bind_rows(day0_by_slice[[d0]] %>% mutate(grp = "A"),
                    day9_by_slice[[d9]] %>% mutate(grp = "B"))
  S <- three_step(datp, CFG, query_rows = gt$origin, col_order = col_order_d9)
  if (is.null(S)) return(tibble())
  pmap_dfr(gt, function(origin, cognate, compartment) {
    r  <- row_rank(S, origin, cognate)
    re <- row_rank_excl(S, origin, cognate, origin)   # drop same-name persister
    tibble(
      d0 = d0, d9 = d9, origin = origin, cognate = cognate, compartment = compartment,
      rank = unname(r["rank"]), n_cand = unname(r["n"]), sim = unname(r["sim"]),
      norm_rank = ifelse(is.finite(r["rank"]) & r["n"] > 1,
                         (r["rank"] - 1) / (r["n"] - 1), NA_real_),
      rank_excl = unname(re["rank"]), n_excl = unname(re["n"])
    )
  })
})

cat(sprintf("Computed %d slice pairs; %d of %d ground-truth tests are testable (origin & target both >=30 cells).\n",
            nrow(pairs_grid),
            sum(is.finite(paired$rank)),
            nrow(pairs_grid) * nrow(gt)))
```

## Testable coverage per ground-truth pair

```{r coverage}
kable(
  paired %>% group_by(origin, cognate, compartment) %>%
    summarise(testable_pairs = sum(is.finite(rank)),
              of_possible = n(), .groups = "drop"),
  caption = "How many of the (up to) 210 Day0–Day9 slice pairs are testable for each ground-truth linkage (both the Day0 origin and the Day9 target reach >=30 cells)."
)
```

# Main result — rank recovery of ground-truth pairs

```{r summary-table}
summary_tbl <- paired %>% filter(is.finite(rank)) %>%
  group_by(origin, cognate, compartment) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs        = n(),
    cand_range     = paste0(min(n_cand), "-", max(n_cand)),
    median_rank    = median(rank),
    mean_rank      = round(mean(rank), 2),
    mean_norm_rank = round(mean(norm_rank, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    pct_top1       = round(100 * mean(rank == 1)),
    pct_top3       = round(100 * mean(rank <= 3)),
    pct_top5       = round(100 * mean(rank <= 5)),
    # supplementary: rank once the un-polarized same-name persister is removed
    median_rank_no_persister = median(rank_excl, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_top1_no_persister    = round(100 * mean(rank_excl == 1, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(pair = paste0(origin, " → ", cognate)) %>%
  select(pair, compartment, n_pairs, cand_range, median_rank, mean_rank,
         mean_norm_rank, pct_top1, pct_top3, pct_top5,
         median_rank_no_persister, pct_top1_no_persister)

kable(summary_tbl,
      caption = "Ground-truth recovery across all testable Day0–Day9 slice pairs. rank/norm_rank = row-wise position of the cognate Day9 target among ALL Day9 candidates (1 = best; norm 0 = best, 1 = worst). pct_topK = % of slice pairs where the cognate is within top K. Last two columns show rank after removing the un-polarized same-name Day9 persister (orientation only).")
```

```{r headline, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat("**Headline.** For each linkage, the cognate Day9 target's standing among *all* Day9 fibroblast/IAF candidates, pooled over the paired slices:\n\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(summary_tbl))) {
  s <- summary_tbl[i, ]
  cat(sprintf("- **%s** (%s): median rank %s of ~%s candidates, normalized rank %.2f, Top-3 in **%d%%** and Top-5 in **%d%%** of %d slice pairs.\n",
              s$pair, s$compartment, s$median_rank, sub("-.*", "", s$cand_range),
              s$mean_norm_rank, s$pct_top3, s$pct_top5, s$n_pairs))
}
```

# Visualizing all 210 paired comparisons

```{r grid-heatmap, fig.width=10, fig.height=11}
paired %>%
  mutate(gt_pair = paste0(origin, " → ", cognate),
         gt_pair = factor(gt_pair, levels = paste0(gt$origin, " → ", gt$cognate)),
         d0 = factor(d0, levels = rev(day0_slices)),
         d9 = factor(d9, levels = day9_slices)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(d9, d0, fill = norm_rank)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.finite(rank), rank, "")), size = 2.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ gt_pair, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#1a9850", high = "#f7f7f7", na.value = "grey88",
                      limits = c(0, 1), name = "norm_rank\n(0=best)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.grid = element_blank()) +
  labs(title = "Cognate Day9 target rank across all Day0 × Day9 slice pairs",
       subtitle = "Rows = Day0 slice, Columns = Day9 slice; number = row-wise rank among all Day9 candidates (lower = better); green = good.",
       x = "Day9 (DSS) slice", y = "Day0 (Healthy) slice")
```

```{r dist-plots, fig.width=9, fig.height=4.5}
pd <- paired %>% filter(is.finite(norm_rank)) %>%
  mutate(gt_pair = factor(paste0(origin, " → ", cognate),
                          levels = paste0(gt$origin, " → ", gt$cognate)))

ggplot(pd, aes(gt_pair, norm_rank, fill = gt_pair)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.5, color = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.16, outlier.size = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of normalized rank of the cognate target across slice pairs",
       subtitle = "0 (top) = cognate is the single best Day9 match; higher = lower in the ranked list.",
       x = NULL, y = "Normalized rank (0 best → 1 worst)")

ggplot(pd, aes(rank, fill = gt_pair)) +
  geom_bar() +
  facet_wrap(~ gt_pair, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:16) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Raw row-wise rank of the cognate Day9 target (count of slice pairs)",
       x = "Rank among all Day9 candidates (1 = best)", y = "Number of slice pairs")
```

# Interpretation and caveats

```{r interp, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
cat('
**Reading the result.** The method "recovers" a ground-truth linkage to the
extent that the cognate Day9 target sits near the top of the Day0 origin\'s
row-wise ranking among *all* Day9 fibroblast/IAF candidates, consistently across
the paired slices (low median/normalized rank, high Top-3/Top-5 rates in the
table and the green-dominated grid rows).

**Caveats:**

1. *Persister ceiling on rank 1.* Day9 still contains un-polarized Fibro 6/2/7,
   which are spatially near-identical to their Day0 selves and therefore usually
   occupy rank 1 in their own row. The cognate IAF can then be at best rank 2 even
   under perfect recovery. The `*_no_persister` columns show the rank once that
   same-name column is removed; the grid/Top-K use the full candidate set as
   requested.
2. *1-D crypt resolution.* In MU, IAF2 (r≈0.47) and IAF4 (r≈0.53) differ by only
   ~0.06, so the two crypt IAFs are harder to separate and per-pair rank is
   noisier for Fibro 6/Fibro 2 than for the layer-separated Fibro 7 → Fibro 4.
3. *Coverage.* IAF4 clears the >=30-cell bar in fewer Day9 slices, so the
   Fibro 2 → IAF4 linkage is evaluated on fewer of the 210 pairs (see coverage).
4. *Spatial, not lineage.* High rank supports the spatial prediction of the
   published polarization; it is co-localization evidence, not lineage proof
   (which the paper establishes by Cxcl12 tracing).
')
```
